title: Case 401

plan.situation: Mr Nowak's 2 pallets (AWB 999-4812 0377) are in Aerovanta's bonded shed B at GDN on customs hold. Duty has been paid. The veterinary inspector is at the shed today between 13:30 and 15:00 CEST. The broker expects his written protocol by about 16:30, and if it is clean the release takes about 30 minutes more. On 8 Oct the desk promised Mr Nowak the inspection outcome and the delivery plan by 17:00 CEST today. He is now chasing angrily. He wants an exact truck time before 14:00, threatens his lawyer and online reviews, and asks for his freight money back.

facts.fact: Cargo landed 06 Oct 22:10, 2 pcs / 412 kg, bonded shed B, status CUSTOMS HOLD; release needs customs plus veterinary inspectorate sign-off
Entry lodged, duty PLN 1,312.40 paid from deposit; broker cannot give a release time until the inspector's protocol
Desk promised the customer the inspection outcome and delivery plan by Fri 9 Oct 17:00 CEST
Inspector at shed B 13:30-15:00 CEST today; protocol usually by 16:30; if clean, ~30 min to release stamp, then Aerovanta can load; broker will forward on arrival
Customer demands exact delivery hour before 14:00 today or a freight refund; threatens lawyer, airline director, Google reviews

missing_information: Veterinary inspection result and written protocol (expected by about 16:30 CEST)
Release stamp time and Aerovanta loading/delivery slot to Straszyn (only possible after a clean protocol)
Who issued the freight invoice and what the refund terms are, needed only if the refund demand is pursued
risk_flags: Legal threat and threat of public reviews: pressure, not a new fact; it does not change the wait test
Self-set 14:00 deadline is not a real cutoff
Refund demand: the desk must not promise any refund or compensation it has not been given
Must not invent a delivery hour before the inspector's protocol exists
Storage charges may start from 12 Oct if release slips (event 002)

authority_map.controls: Customs entry, release stamp, forwarding the protocol
Release from shed B, loading, storage charges

authority_map.party: Freight invoicing party (not identified in record)
authority_map.controls: Any freight refund; no pre-authorisation recorded
Whether to keep or cancel his order

wait_check.new_since_last_promise: Nothing material. Event 006 confirms the inspection window is on track. Event 007 brings anger, a lawyer threat, a self-set 14:00 deadline and a refund demand, but no new fact.
wait_check.pending_promise: Desk to the customer: outcome and delivery plan by Fri 9 Oct 17:00 CEST. Broker: protocol usually by 16:30 CEST, release about 30 min after a clean result. Inspector on site 13:30-15:00 CEST today.

plan.decision_summary: Hold: the inspection is under way inside its window and the desk's 17:00 CEST promise still stands, so send nothing now, record the chase, and check for the protocol at 16:30 CEST so the promised update goes out by 17:00.
plan.rationale: Event 007 is a chase with threats and no new fact. The inspection is happening inside its confirmed window, and the owners' times (protocol about 16:30, desk update 17:00) are still ahead. No delivery hour exists until the protocol and release exist. A message now could only repeat 'working on it' or invent a time, and the customer has explicitly rejected the first. The refund demand is not something the desk controls or can promise. It can be raised with the invoicing party later if he formally pursues it after the 17:00 update.

actions.body: 13:52 CEST 9 Oct: customer chase (event 007) demanding exact delivery hour before 14:00 or freight refund; threatens lawyer/airline director/Google reviews. No new fact. Inspector on site at shed B 13:30-15:00 CEST (event 006); protocol expected ~16:30 CEST; release ~30 min after clean result. Desk promise to customer: outcome + delivery plan by 17:00 CEST today (event 005). Holding: no hour or refund to give yet. Note: storage free only until 12 Oct (event 002). Refund demand to be handled only via the invoicing party if pursued; nothing promised.
actions.purpose: Log the chase and the reason for holding

actions.body: Check whether Ewa Sawicka (Baltic Clear Customs) has forwarded the vet protocol and release status for AWB 999-4812 0377. If clean, get the release stamp and ask Aerovanta GDN import for the loading/delivery slot. Send Mr Nowak the promised outcome and plan by 17:00 CEST using only confirmed facts. If there is no protocol yet, write to Mr Nowak by 17:00 CEST anyway with the factual status and no invented time, and ask Ewa Sawicka for the protocol status. Address his refund demand neutrally without promising anything.
actions.purpose: Meet the 17:00 CEST promise to the customer using the broker's expected protocol time

not_doing: Not replying now with a delivery hour: none exists until the protocol and release exist, and inventing one would break status precision
Not sending another 'we are working on it' message: the customer rejected it and it adds nothing
Not promising or refusing a freight refund: the desk does not control it and no authority is recorded
Not escalating on the lawyer threat: a threat is not a new fact and nothing irreversible is pending
Not chasing the broker or inspector: they are inside their stated windows
plan.follow_up: At 16:30 CEST (14:30 UTC) today, check for the vet protocol and release from Ewa Sawicka. By 17:00 CEST, send Mr Nowak the outcome and delivery plan, or the factual status if the protocol is late. If the protocol has not arrived by 17:00, ask Ewa Sawicka for its status and flag the 12 Oct storage-charge start to Aerovanta.

review.summary: The hold is correct. The customer's message adds no new fact, only pressure, a deadline he set himself and a refund demand. The inspector is on site inside the confirmed 13:30–15:00 window, the protocol is expected by about 16:30, and the desk's 17:00 CEST promise has not come due yet. The plan sends nothing outbound, invents no delivery time and promises no refund. The follow-up at 16:30 CEST (14:30 UTC) is converted correctly and is timed to meet the 17:00 promise.
